interest: Illuminates Japanese officer interrogations on Southeast Asian mineral exploitation and early Cold War tracking of uranium and beryllium.
overview: This file documents Allied and U.S. policies regarding Japanese base metals, mineral resources, and metallurgical industries between 1946 and 1949. It details export pricing and international allocations of stockpiled antimony, copper, lead, and tin to Allied nations; SCAP technical reports on Japan's wartime tungsten, molybdenum, and ferroalloy metallurgy; and assessments of regional mineral resources, including bauxite deposits in the Palau Islands and wartime discoveries along the Burma-Siam Railroad drawn from interrogations of repatriated Japanese commanders. Later records address Far Eastern Commission light metals reparations policy, commercial proposals to process imported alumina, and security measures concerning strategic and radioactive materials such as impounded uranium oxide, beryllium, and titanium.
